review_comments:
This seems to be incorrect as well, there is no error handling here?

What is the command fails?

Hi @frenck ,
you mean `what if the command fails`?

In that case, there is little or nothing we can do if the command fails due to API call (let's say, due to network error or panel busy state). I think the best we handle this case is simply let the user know that the command failed and let the user try again, which is something already happens with the current implementation. Don't you agree?

> In that case, there is little or nothing we can do if the command fails due to API call (let's say, due to network error or panel busy state).

Sure, but do we need to handle it? As this is unhandled right now if used in an automation and the call fails; the automation will just be marked as "Successfully ran" (which is not true).

Also, there will be no feedback to the user. From the user's perspective, everything worked.

So, IMHO, that is wrong and should be added.

I think I am missing your point.
Let me try to clarify.

The current version of the method is the following:
```python
    async def async_alarm_disarm(self, code: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Send disarm command."""
        # Elmax alarm panels do always require a code to be passed for disarm operations
        if code is None or code == "":
            raise ValueError("Please input the disarm code.")
        await self.coordinator.http_client.execute_command(
            endpoint_id=self._device.endpoint_id,
            command=AreaCommand.DISARM,
            extra_payload={"code": code},
        )
        await self.coordinator.async_refresh()
```

If the user does not specify a code, a `ValueError` is raised and shown at UI; so the execution stops with an error. In here, there is no error handling we can do rather than telling the user he must use a disarm code.

The rest of the method simply invokes the `execute_command()` instructions of the `http_client` object, which is exposed by the coordinator. This object is an `Elmax` API helper object ([ref here](https://github.com/albertogeniola/elmax-api/blob/f0000078bd08e5d6c76bef37a4e0b070fd13b4ba/elmax_api/http.py#L345)). In particular the method `execute_command()` ([ref here](https://github.com/albertogeniola/elmax-api/blob/f0000078bd08e5d6c76bef37a4e0b070fd13b4ba/elmax_api/http.py#451)) handles the communication with the API within the internal `_internal_request` method ([ref here](https://github.com/albertogeniola/elmax-api/blob/f0000078bd08e5d6c76bef37a4e0b070fd13b4ba/elmax_api/http.py#L158)). This method will raise the corresponding exception based on the specific error that occurs. Such exceptions aren't caught by the `async_alarm_disarm` method (they are not silenced in any way, as far as I can tell), so they will propagate to the caller (HA/Script executor). Thus, I doubt the automation will mark it as `Successfully ran`, or am I wrong?

About the feedback, yes it will be given as an exception is generated. Maybe wen can trap the 401/403 and show a more convenient "Invalid Code" message? Is this what you mean?

> Thus, I doubt the automation will mark it as Successfully ran, or am I wrong?

Yes, only Home Assistant errors are handled. In this case, it will not throw that, it will throw something else.
